probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: A and B are equally convenient and priced, and each satisfies a different plausible bundle of personal considerations. The decisive distinction requires applying the one-bed queen default together with the early-morning work-room amenity scope, rather than treating a larger bed or a full recovery-amenity package as generically dominant.
probes.gold_action: Lead with the confirmed queen studio with in-room coffee and mini-fridge.
probes.label_rationale: The query alone leaves A and B genuinely unresolved: they tie on price, rating, walk, and cancellation, while early-start room basics compete with recovery facilities. History resolves that tradeoff. Kara repeatedly requests a queen when it is selectable for work travel (s0005, s0015), pairs a queen with confirmed coffee and refrigerator access for early work mornings (s0039, s0083), and has treated a hot tub as a soft benefit when room basics are covered (s0000). A king is acceptable when it is what is available, but the history does not support automatically replacing an available queen with a king. A also avoids any price, timing, or convenience sacrifice relative to B.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: the closest alternative offers a king, a materially higher guest rating, and better in-room conveniences, while the gold offers the recovery bundle and the queen default. Neither option is generically dominant, and resolving the conflict requires recognizing both the limited king exception and the active-recovery scope of the amenities preference.
probes.gold_action: Lead with the queen cottage that confirms the pool, hot tub, and fitness access.
probes.label_rationale: A and B are deliberately comparable on rate, access, and cancellation: A offers the recovery facilities that fit this trip, while B offers a higher review score and more convenient in-room food-and-drink setup. Kara has said a queen is enough and a king is not necessary when a queen is available (s0011), and has accepted that a king can be fine in a particular resort context (s0052) rather than treating it as forbidden. That makes B a real alternative, not a throwaway. But the history supports a queen as the default shared-bed selection, and A also matches her active-recovery pool/hot-tub/fitness preference. Its 4.2 guest rating clears her usual rating floor; B's higher rating is a bonus, not a reason to auto-upgrade the bed type. The record also treats missing recovery amenities as something to state plainly rather than ignore (s0032), while s0118 confirms that queen-versus-king is context-sensitive rather than a universal king preference.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: B offers a higher guest rating and all three recovery amenities at identical price and shuttle access, whereas A offers the recurring queen setup and early-work room basics. The correct choice depends on the scoped one-bed policy plus the early-morning hotel-amenity pattern, not on any query-stated generic rule.
probes.gold_action: Lead with the confirmed queen studio with in-room coffee and a mini-fridge.
probes.label_rationale: The prompt does not establish whether early-morning room basics or a higher-rated full recovery-amenity package matters more, so A and B remain plausible without history. The history resolves it toward A: Kara has explicitly rejected doubles for these sorts of stays (s0009) and refused a double-bed substitution merely to gain a practical benefit (s0021). She also repeatedly seeks a queen plus confirmed in-room coffee and mini-fridge for early work travel (s0039, s0072). The better rating and pool/hot-tub bundle in B are meaningful soft considerations, but s0000 shows that room basics can take priority over a hot tub. A ties B on price, shuttle, and cancellation, so the gold does not use the queen preference to override a generic cost or convenience disadvantage.
